newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks close lower, Nomura impact limited.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks close lower, Nomura impact limited.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed lower on Friday, weighed down by profit-taking sales of issues that had risen earlier in the day. Players were discouraged by an absence of usual month-end buying to support the market.

News that Tokyo prosecutors had arrested Nomura Securities Co's former president in connection with a widening scandal involving suspected illegal payoffs to a racketeer had only a limited impact on the market, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average lost 243.42 points or 1.20 percent to close at 20,068.81. June Nikkei futures fell 170 points to 20,140.
Trading of the 225 issues in the Nikkei was volatile, especially late on. It ranged between 20,029.10 and 20,390.44.
"An absence of end-month buying discouraged dealers and prompted them to unload longs," one broker said.

"Many people opt to sell stocks on the Nikkei's rally above 20,000," said Kiyoshi Kimura, general manager of research at Societe Generale Securities. He said lingering worries over the yen's rise capped leading exporters.
Shares of Nomura slipped on news that of former president's arrest. But the losses were limited, as brokers said the news had been mostly factored in by the market.
Nomura shares shed 60 yen to close at 1,380.

"The news had been largely anticipated. Unless the scandal widens and politicians who are rumoured to be involved are arrested, the impact is likely to be limited," said Kunihiro Hatae, general manager at Tokyo Securities Co Ltd.

Nomura president Junichi Ujiie said on Friday he would not deny the possibility that the Japanese brokerage itself had been involved in a racketeer payoff scandal if the firm was so accused. The Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) said on Friday it would deal "in a strict manner" with the case of Nomura, depending on the outcome of investigations into the scandal.
The TSE's first-section turnover was 422 million shares on Friday, up from 364 million on Thursday. Losers outstripped gainers 607 to 486, while 146 issues were unchanged.
In other indices, the broader-based TOPIX index slipped 16.45 points or 1.09 percent to end at 1,486.89. The Nikkei 300 average fell 4.28 points or 1.47 percent to 286.54.

Analysts expected stocks to remain in a consolidation phase next week, as continuing hopes of a money inflow from public funds are likely to make the floor solid, while gains will be limited due to an unclear outlook on currencies and possible corrective falls in Wall Street stocks.
By sector, decliners were led by gas, shipbuilding, pulp/paper, air transport and fisheries. The notable advancing sectors were services, communications, and credit/lease.
Shares of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp shot up to end at 1.11 million yen, a new high for this calendar year, helped by a foreign securities house's massive buying.
Brokers said the telecommunications giant's inclusion in Morgan Stanley Capital International's Japan index continued to support the share price.
Some high-technology shares, especially Sony Corp, surged, but they later retreated due to profit-taking.
Shortly after the session opened, Sony shares jumped to a new record high of 10,000 yen as domestic and foreign investors as well as investment trusts snapped up the shares.
But the shares lost 30 yen to close at 9,810.
Some other high-tech issues also shed earlier gains.
TDK Corp ended 110 yen lower at 8,940, after posting healthy gains.
Fujitsu Ltd, ranked as the most heavily traded issue with turnover of 10.546 million shares, also rose during the session but closed unchanged at 1,420.
The second section index was up 9.55 points at 1,786.81, with 10.72 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was up 4.94 points at 1,187.53.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
